text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to #incidents: High rate of 429 responses observed during rl_v2 canary rollout in us-west-2. Error spike at 12:33 UTC, elevated token-accounting mismatches reported. Paging SRE oncall + eng-runtime.

sre-oncall: ack — I'm on it. Pulling up dashboards, traces, and the rate-limiter config. Can someone confirm which rollout ID is active?

alejandra: rl_v2_canary (rollout id: ro-2026-03-15-09). Canary weight at 15%. Seeing 429s concentrated on requests with exempt=false header. Exemption table queries are returning empty for some keys.

ben: I just saw DeployBot show a canary promotion step at 12:30. Noted a config change to ratecap exemptions in the same patch. Reverting canary flag now.

ben: executing rollback: ```
# disable canary
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane/redwood/feature_flags/rl_v2_canary -d '{"enabled": false}'
``` 

deploy-bot: canary rollback request accepted, starting rollback workflow. Will post status updates.

alejandra: while rollback runs, we should hotfix rate-limit exemptions. The exemption lookup query was refactored to use a new token_id field; some production token rows still use legacy_id.

tas: I can patch quick. Proposed mitigation: re-add legacy_id fallback to exemption lookup and flip a runtime flag. Patch snippet: ```sql
-- add fallback join
LEFT JOIN token_aliases ta ON ta.legacy_id = tokens.id OR ta.new_id = tokens.id
``` Applying in read-only safe mode.

eng-runtime: we should also toggle a kill-switch to stop strict per-key throttling and fall back to global bucket while we patch. Kill-switch: `rate.limit.strict_per_key = false`.

sre-oncall: agree. Ben, can you apply the kill-switch? I want to minimize customer impact while we fix accounting.

ben: applying kill-switch now: ```
kubectl -n infra exec -it rl-rate-limiter-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'ratelimitctl set strict_per_key false && ratelimitctl reload'
``` done. Observability: tokens/429s dropping in 60s.

support-lead: support triage — initial estimate: ~2-4% of requests impacted for top 20 customers in us-west-2 between 12:30-12:45 UTC. Customers A & D saw spikes in error rates. Notifying affected accounts now.

product-ops: tagging incident as "release-related: ratecap regression" in incident tracker. Adding timeline and start time.

alejandra: rolling a targeted db fallback to restore exemptions for legacy tokens. Command: ```
PATCH /internal/exemptions/refresh?mode=fallback
``` will rehydrate cache from legacy table.

ben: exemption cache refresh in progress. Cache warm completed. Monitoring.

sre-oncall: good. Can we validate token-accounting? I'm running an audit query comparing pre-deploy and post-deploy token sums.

eng-runtime: audit shows token balance drift for ~0.6% of tokens — mostly tokens created in last 48h that only had new_id populated. Our refactor missed populating legacy_id for those tokens.

tas: quick fix pushed to service that reads both id fields until we migrate all tokens. Deploying as hotfix to canary groups not being rolled out (small safe rollout to rate-limiter nodes).

deploy-bot: hotfix deployment started to rl-exemptions-service (hotfix/hybrid-id-support). Canary to 3 pods.

ben: I'm going to stay on until the handoff. tas — want the overnight on-call after 13:15 UTC? I'll do a summary and handoff once metrics are green for 15m.

tas: I can take the handoff. Please include runbook link and current mitigation state.

sre-oncall: current mitigation summary: 1) canary disabled (flag off) 2) rate-limit strict per-key kill-switch off -> global throttling 3) exemption cache rehydrated from legacy table 4) hotfix deployed to support both id columns. Customer impact reduced to near-zero; 429s dropped to baseline.

ben: creating handoff note: ```
Handoff for tas @ 13:20 UTC
- Incident: ratecap regressions after rl_v2 canary deploy
- Actions taken: canary flag disabled, strict_per_key disabled, exemption cache refresh, hotfix deployed
- Current status: stable for 18m, 95th token error rate ~baseline
- Next steps: monitor token-accounting audits (audit job id: audit-1823459), verify full token migration in next 72h, schedule rollback of kill-switch after migration
- Links: https://dashboards.redwood/alerts/1823459, https://runbooks.redwood/ratecap-rollback
``` 

tas: acknowledging handoff. I'll monitor for 2 hours and coordinate with Product & Support if we see any regression.

support-lead: support messages to customers sent for impacted accounts; proactive outreach scheduled for EOD. Recording incident severity P2 -> review for possible P1 if metrics spike again.

product-ops: adding postmortem owner: alejandro (APM) and timeline owner: ben. Please create preliminary postmortem doc within 24h.

alejandra: will start collecting relevant logs and diff of exemption query behavior; also collecting the small set of token rows missing legacy_id for migration.

tas: quick question — do we want to keep strict_per_key=false during migration or re-enable with a more conservative threshold? leaning to keep off until token migration completes to avoid repeated customer blips.

sre-oncall: agree keep off. Add automated check to re-enable only when audit shows zero drift for 24h across all regions.

ben: final note — we need a follow-up to ensure rollout processes include an exemption schema migration step. Adding to eng-runtime backlog.

incident-bot: incident closed: mitigation successful, monitoring active. Summary and postmortem requested.

support-lead: :thumbsup: closing thread for now. Will reopen if anything pops up.
